common_instruction: This is a response-only exercise. Use the supplied scenario and snippets; propose or review the requested work without claiming files were changed, commands ran, or external systems were inspected. State material verification limits. Equivalent solutions that satisfy the stated contract are acceptable.

cases.name: catalog-entry-is-not-current-production-qualification
cases.prompt: You are choosing a Go message broker client for a production service. The local catalogue names two third-party libraries, but includes no verified maintenance date, license, supported Go version, or vulnerability information. The service needs explicit cancellation and the existing broker protocol; the standard library does not implement that protocol. No network or live package lookup is available in this exercise. Give a useful decision path and state what you can recommend now.
expectations: Uses the required protocol/cancellation and compatibility constraints to form a bounded shortlist or evaluation plan.
Identifies maintenance, license, supported version/API, and security evidence still needed from primary package sources.
Keeps any library preference conditional and does not invent current qualification facts.
Does not dismiss a necessary protocol library merely because standard-library-first is a general preference.
negative_expectations: Must not certify either catalogue entry as currently maintained, vulnerability-free, licensed compatibly, or production-ready without evidence.
Must not fabricate API signatures, release versions, or a completed package lookup.
cases.trap: Treat a recommendation catalogue as fresh verified evidence about a dependency.

cases.name: stdlib-covers-small-json-http-client
cases.prompt: A small Go command sends one HTTP POST containing a fixed JSON struct, uses a timeout, checks the response status, and decodes a JSON response. It needs no retries, middleware, schema generation, authentication SDK, or special transport. The repo has no HTTP client dependency. Recommend the smallest dependency choice and explain the request/response responsibilities it still must handle.
expectations: Chooses standard-library HTTP and JSON support as sufficient for the stated task.
Retains timeout/cancellation, response-body closure, status handling, and decode-error handling as the actual responsibilities.
Makes additional dependencies contingent on a concrete missing capability.
negative_expectations: Must not add an HTTP framework/client wrapper or generation stack just because it appears in the catalogue.
Must not equate using the standard library with being able to omit error handling or resource cleanup.
cases.trap: Recommend a popular wrapper for a case already served by a small explicit standard-library client.
